# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 61 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 47 | Coptic

---

## Saying 61

Jesus said: "Two will rest upon a bed; one will die, one will live." Salome said: "Who are you, man, that you have come up upon my couch and eaten from my table?" Jesus said to her: "I am the one who comes from what is whole. I was given from the things of my Father." "I am your disciple." "Therefore I say: When someone becomes whole, he will be filled with light. But when he becomes divided, he will be filled with darkness."

---

**Translator's Notes (EMET):**

- The saying opens with a Q-parallel (Luke 17:34) but immediately becomes a dialogue unique to Thomas
- **Salome** — one of only two named women in Thomas (with Mary in 114)
- **ⲁⲛⲅ ⲡⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ ϩⲙ ⲡⲉⲧϫⲏⲕ** / "I am the one who comes from what is whole" — *petjek*: whole, complete, undivided
- The dialogue is fragmented; it is unclear who speaks "I am your disciple" — most likely Salome responding to Jesus
- **ⲣⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ** / light vs. **ⲕⲁⲕⲉ** / darkness — the dualistic conclusion
- "Couch" (*klinē*) — dining couch, reclining posture for meals
